title: France and allies are preparing a «defensive» mission to restore shipping in the Strait of Hormuz — Forbes.ua
snippet: Paris and its allies are preparing a «defensive» mission to restore shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. This was stated by French President Emmanuel Macron, Le Monde reports. Details The mission will be purely defensive in nature and will be aimed at escorting container ships and oil tankers in order to gradually restore the key maritime route after the acute phase of the conflict in the Middle East. The mission will be sent to escort tankers «after the end of the most acute phase of the conflict», Macron said. Macron noted that the opening of the strait is critical for international trade and gas and oil supplies. Several European and extra-European states plan to take part in the mission. The operation will involve an aircraft carrier «Charles de Gaulle», as well as eight frigates and two amphibious helicopter carriers. Context Due to the escalation of the conflict in the Middle East, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz fell by about 90%. About a fifth of the world's oil supplies and a significant share of liquefied natural gas trade pass through this route. The United Arab Emirates, Kuwait and Iraq have already reduced oil production as storage facilities quickly fill due to the virtual closure of the Strait of Hormuz. On March 9, the price of Brent oil approached $120 per barrel amid the escalation of the conflict. title: Baghaei's Iranian Foreign Ministry called the Strait of Hormuz unsafe for navigation
snippet: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei stressed that the Strait of Hormuz has become unsafe for navigation due to US and Israeli military actions in the Middle East. In an interview with RT, he indicated that the current conflict is directed not only against Tehran, but also against the entire region as a whole. «The United States is using its military bases and fleets in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, as well as other places, to attack Iran», — Baghaei noted. In response to this, Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth previously said that the United States has the necessary capabilities to protect shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: US vows to secure Strait of Hormuz as tensions with Iran continue - What's happening?
snippet: Amid ongoing tensions in West Asia, the United States has reportedly stated that it will ensure the security of the Strait of Hormuz and maintain the free flow of global energy supplies. Meanwhile, as global oil prices surge, triggered by escalating conflict in the region, US President Donald Trump said the "short-term" spike is worth the cost if it eliminates Tehran's nuclear threat. In a post on Truth Social, Trump argued that oil prices would "drop rapidly" once Iran's nuclear capabilities are destroyed, adding that "only fools would think differently." On the other hand, according to IANS, in an interview with CBS's 60 Minutes, US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth emphasised that American forces were already degrading Iran's naval capabilities and were prepared to take further action to safeguard critical shipping routes. He also added that the US forces would continue targeting vessels and assets that threaten maritime security. He suggested that Washington's military operations were aimed at ensuring that such disruptions do not materialise. title: iranian Foreign Ministry: The US and Israel are making the Strait of Hormuz unsafe - Tsargrad
snippet: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Esmail Baghaei said that the Strait of Hormuz has become unsafe for navigation due to the actions of the US and Israel. US President Donald Trump warns of possible consequences if oil supplies are cut off. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said the Strait of Hormuz had become unsafe for navigation due to the war waged by the United States and Israel in the Middle East. In his commentary to RT, he emphasized that this conflict is directed not only against Tehran, but also against the entire region. The United States is using all these military bases, using its fleets in the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman and other places to carry out attacks on Iran," Bagai noted. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth previously emphasized that the United States has the ability to protect shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. US President Donald Trump assured that if oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz are stopped, Iran will suffer 20 times more. In addition, he mentioned the possibility of accepting the Strait of Hormuz under US control. We previously wrote about the tense situation between Iran and the United States, as well as the threat voiced by the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to stop oil exports to the United States and Israel. Against the backdrop of these events, strikes began on Iranian targets on February 28, which provoked retaliatory actions on Israeli territory and on US military bases, emphasizing the escalation of the conflict in the region.
